subject: [hw] T01 -> lead: V19 VMOVN/VSHN decode is wrong (clean 1-instruction repro); V19 is finished
body:
Another clean class bug, this time V19s narrow decode. Repro (thumb, current tree, asmrun):

  movw r4,#0x5678; movt r4,#0x1234; vdup.32 q0,r4
  vmovn.i16 d1,q0        @ ffb21200; expected d1 = 5678 5678 (low 16 of each 32-bit lane), got 3478 3478

llvm-mc shows the narrow encodings: vmovn.i16 q->d = ffb21200, vmovn.i32 = ffb60222, vmovn.i64 = ffba0432; vshrn.i16 #4 = ef8c1648, vshrn.i32 #8 = ef981858. n2a32_neon_shift.c computes `imm7 = (N<<6) | bits21-16` and then selects the source element size by the ranges imm7<16/32/64. For vmovn.i16 imm7 is 0x32=50, so it is decoded as a 64-bit source and shifts by 14 -> 3478. The narrow element size is encoded by the `size` field, not by those imm7 ranges (the range model works for the right/left shifts but not for opc 8/9). This is likely the root of k_i8_loop/k_i16_loop/k_i16_mul/k_neon_vsubl/k_neon_vmla16 failing at arm-O2/O3v: all use vmovn.i16/i32, and my isolated k_neon_vmovn only passed because its data happened to survive. V18s k18_select (all seeds) is VEXT instead (separate message to V20).
Suggested fix: decode size=(insn>>18)&3 for opc 8/9, map src_esize=32<<size (size 1,2,3), and derive the shift from the imm6 low bits (`imm6 = bits21-16`, shift = src_esize - imm6 for VSHN? please verify with llvm-mc: for vmovn.i16 (src32, shift0) imm6=0x32=50, so the relation is not the simple src-shift you documented). I can supply a table of all five encodings and expected lane results if useful. No phone.
